relevance_note: Symposium review of SSADH deficiency that, besides group-level database tables, gives individual-level details for a few people, e.g. 'Her living sister ... She has an Aldh5A1 mutation (p.Gly409Asp).'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values. Tables 1-5 are group counts only (N=60 questionnaire database; N=35 adolescents/adults) and give no individual rows; the 33-patient Knerr et al 2008a cohort, the 10 polysomnography patients, 7 FMZ-PET patients, 8 TMS families and the 5 NIH patients with symmetric pallidal/dentate/subthalamic signal are group-level only and get no rows. Individuals: two adolescent brothers (Leuzzi et al 2007), a single polysomnography patient (Arnulf et al 2005; SSADH diagnosis implied by context only, not stated for the person), a 19-year-old decedent and her living sister (Knerr et al 2008b; decedent labelled by rule 4, sister by rule 2), two NIH-protocol patients described first-hand in the neuroimaging paragraph (one with asymmetric pallidal involvement, the oldest aged 27; diagnosis implied by context), and a 2 1/2-year-old boy treated with taurine (Saronwala et al 2008). Leuzzi disease label taken from the reference-list title. The decedent's postmortem diagnosis was 'epilepsy of unknown aetiology' and SSADH deficiency was assigned retrospectively; her DNA analysis was 'in progress', so she has no variant row. The sister's variant p.Gly409Asp is printed protein-only, with no zygosity or inheritance; sister's 'borderline cognition (IQ = 70)' not mapped to the intellectual disability checklist item. Oldest NIH patient's 'pallidal signal abnormality' does not state T2, so the T2 checklist item is left not reported; 'clear volume loss' is not localized, so atrophy is not reported. The boy's insomnia occurred at higher taurine doses (treatment-associated), recorded as observed. The boy's age (2 1/2 years) is the age as described in the report, possibly at treatment start. No contradictions found.
